rv.q: When Lear’s heart broke, so did mine.
I would urge you to see this to see this excellent production...
Ian McDiarmid returns to the Crucible to play in a ponderous production of Shakespeare’s tragedy
Titas Halder's production for Sheffield Crucible is efficient, but undistinguished, raised to another level by one performance only, Ian McDiarmid as Lear.
A compelling, stunning production of Shakespeare's most uncompromising tragedy, with impeccable performances throughout, especially from the hugely impressive Ian McDiarmid in the title role.
McDiarmid’s Lear is a phenomenal accomplishment that you feel privileged to be witnessing.
This production brings a modern, creative touch, while still holding true to the original material.
This is a darkly compelling interpretation of one of Shakespeare’s most celebrated tragedies, anchored by a memorable lead performance from McDiarmid.
His portrayal of Lear is one of the greatest I have ever seen.
The play spirals towards a finale of war and death and misery in a play that is debatably Shakespeare’s greatest work. The cast is generally very good.
Arresting from the start, this is a stunning, engrossing and totally lucid production, full of fine performances and intense atmosphere.
You don't need to be a Shakespeare expert to appreciate great theatre — and this production proves that.
Though King Lear is a tough watch for me a first-timer, meanwhile the effort in its design and direction delivers something likeable.
